ModuleName: 3 - Use Case Scenarios and Requirements Gathering
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's topics covering use case scenarios, stakeholder identification, requirements gathering techniques, and task analysis, used by instructors to plan lessons and by learners to navigate the module's scope.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: This HTML page lists and briefly describes the topics covered in Module 3, including an introduction to Use Case Scenarios and their role in software development, giving learners and instructors an overview of what the module will teach before diving into the material.

Artifacts.Name: Use Case Scenarios & Requirements Specification
Artifacts.Description: An HTML-formatted group assignment brief instructing student teams to produce a use case scenarios and requirements specification document, including effort estimates, AI use policy, and submission guidance, used by students to understand deliverables and by instructors to distribute the task.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to Use Case Scenarios
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces use case scenarios as a structured narrative technique for capturing user-system interactions, explaining why they exist, what they contain, and how development teams use them to bridge the gap between stakeholder intent and what is actually built.

Artifacts.Name: Identifying Stakeholders and Users
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to identify the full range of stakeholders and users connected to a system — including internal roles, external partners, and regulators — and guides learners through the process of mapping who cares about a system before any requirements or use cases are written.

Artifacts.Name: Requirements Gathering Techniques
Artifacts.Description: This reading surveys the major requirements elicitation methods — such as interviews, workshops, observation, and surveys — describing how each technique works, when to apply it, and how analysts use them together to discover and articulate what a system must do and the qualities it must possess.

Artifacts.Name: Task Analysis
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers task analysis as a systematic method for studying how users actually perform their work, including the sequence of steps, decisions, and goals involved, and explains how analysts use this understanding as a foundation for writing accurate use cases and interface designs.

Artifacts.Name: Writing Use Case Scenarios
Artifacts.Description: This reading provides step-by-step guidance on composing well-formed use case scenarios, covering the roles of actors, the structure of main and alternative flows, preconditions and postconditions, and the craft and discipline required to produce clear, complete scenario documentation.

Artifacts.Name: Enumerating Usage Paths and Edge Cases
Artifacts.Description: This reading addresses how to move beyond the 'happy path' by systematically identifying alternative usage paths, edge cases, and boundary conditions, and explains techniques designers and analysts use to enumerate and account for unexpected user behavior and real-world variability.

Artifacts.Name: Documenting and Communicating Requirements
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to organize, present, and maintain requirements and use case documents for different audiences — including developers, stakeholders, and testers — covering document structure, version control, communication strategies, and keeping documentation accurate as projects evolve.

Artifacts.Name: Documenting and Communicating Requirements
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to organize, present, and maintain requirements and use case documents for different audiences — including developers, stakeholders, and testers — covering document structure, version control, communication strategies, and keeping documentation accurate as projects evolve.

Artifacts.Name: Quiz Question Bank (5 questions)
Artifacts.Description: A five-question matching quiz bank covering use case components and their definitions, flow types, sources of ambiguity in use case steps, use case templates and their origins, and writing guidelines for specific use case sections, used to assess learners' understanding of use case terminology and structure.

Artifacts.Name: Use Case Scenarios & Requirements Specification
Artifacts.Description: A Markdown-formatted version of the same group assignment asking student teams to develop use case scenarios and a requirements specification, covering the same scope, policies, and expectations as the HTML counterpart, used as a portable or LMS-importable alternative for the same task.

Artifacts.Name: Semester Group Project — Phase 2
Artifacts.Description: An HTML assignment sheet for Phase 2 of the semester group project directing student teams to conduct stakeholder analysis, requirements gathering, and use case development as a continuation of Phase 1, used by students to complete their next project milestone and by instructors to assess progress toward the full system design.
